external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and can manually trigger rebuilds.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where developers are located or how they authenticate.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be manually triggered to rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA for the estate and answers release queries from store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call the controller; the token is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small back-office server at each store that checks the current release, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores. Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the registry, or what it presents to the controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The text does not describe the data handled by the till software beyond its delivery as a container image.

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: The Git server where developers push branches and from which the build runner fetches source.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry in the build environment that stores finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and serves pulls from store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN. Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes branches to the self-hosted Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the self-hosted Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.data_description: Source code for the merged branch

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build on the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.
data_flows.data_description: A build trigger associated with a merge to main

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: A finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: make current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: A request containing the image SHA to make current

data_flows.name: look up release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the required image from the image registry when its current image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: The container image for the current release

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner resolves dependencies through the public package registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The lockfile is taken as given, and the runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: Dependency packages selected through the lockfile

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually kicks off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.
data_flows.data_description: A manual rebuild request for main
